stem: What is the purpose of the process of initiating a project?
answer: To establish solid foundations so the business understands the work needed before committing resources
distractors: To appoint the project manager and prepare the outline business case for approval
To authorize each management stage and monitor its progress against the stage plan
To accept the products delivered by team managers and confirm they meet their quality criteria
To confirm that the project product is ready for operational use and hand it over
To prepare the next stage plan whenever a stage boundary is approaching
To define the organization's project management framework and its tailoring
explanation: Initiating a project establishes solid foundations so the business can see the work required to deliver the project product before committing significant expenditure or resources. Appointing the project manager and drafting the outline business case belong to starting up a project, and stage authorization belongs to directing a project.

stem: PRINCE2 says that initiating a project prepares the foundations for a successful project. For genuine commitment, what must all parties be clear about?
answer: What the project will achieve, why it is needed, how it will be achieved and what their responsibilities are
distractors: The cost of every work package, the name of every team member, and the date of every checkpoint report
The supplier's profit margin, the customer's budget, and the payment schedule agreed in the contract
The benefits to be realized in each financial year, the owners of each benefit, and the review dates
The full set of product descriptions, the acceptance criteria for every product, and the quality tolerances
The tolerances that the business layer has set, the escalation routes, and the reporting arrangements for the board
The lessons recorded in the project log, how each has been applied, and who applied it in the stage
explanation: Commitment depends on all parties being clear on what the project is intended to achieve, why it is needed, how the outcome is to be achieved and what their responsibilities are. Detailed cost breakdowns and product-level criteria are developed later in the process, not required for this shared understanding.

stem: Which of these is listed as an objective of the process of initiating a project?
answer: Establishing a common understanding of how baselines will be controlled
distractors: Appointing the project executive and project manager and confirming their availability
Delivering the project product within the tolerances agreed for the first stage
Confirming that the expected benefits have been realized in operational use
Selecting the supplier through a competitive procurement exercise
Approving the end stage report for the initiation stage
Defining the organization's overall risk appetite and risk tolerance
explanation: The objectives of initiating a project are a set of things on which there must be a common understanding, and how baselines will be established and controlled is one of them. Appointing the executive and project manager happens in starting up a project, and benefit realization is confirmed after the project.

stem: Which of these is NOT an objective of the process of initiating a project?
answer: To appoint the project executive and project manager and confirm their availability for the project
distractors: To reach a common understanding of the reasons for the project, the benefits expected and the associated risks
To reach a common understanding of who needs information, in what format and at what time
To reach a common understanding of how the project applies business policies, methods and guidance
explanation: The objectives are shared understandings covering justification, scope, delivery, decision-making, quality, baselines, risks and issues, progress, information needs and the application of business policies. Appointing the executive and project manager is done during starting up a project, before initiation can be authorized.

stem: A project manager is asked to make sure the project follows the corporate sustainability policy and the organization's standard delivery method. Which objective of initiating a project does this address?
answer: The objective of a common understanding of how the project applies business policies and methods
distractors: The objective that there is a common understanding of how baselines will be established and controlled
The objective that there is a common understanding of who is to be involved in project decision-making
The objective that there is a common understanding of how the quality required will be achieved
The objective that there is a common understanding of who needs information, in what format and at what time
The objective that there is a common understanding of how and when products will be delivered and at what cost
The objective that there is a common understanding of the scope of what is to be done
explanation: Aligning the project with corporate policy and a standard delivery method satisfies the objective about applying business policies, methods and guidance. Baseline control, decision-making, quality, communication needs and delivery are separate objectives in the same list.

stem: Which process triggers the process of initiating a project?
answer: Directing a project, by authorizing the initiation stage
distractors: Starting up a project, by approving the project brief
Managing a stage boundary, at the end of the initiation stage
Controlling a stage, when the first delivery stage begins
Managing product delivery, when the first work package is agreed
The business layer, by issuing the project mandate
Closing a project, when the benefits are reviewed
explanation: The input that starts the process is project initiation authorized, which comes from the project board's decision in directing a project. Starting up a project ends by asking the board for that authorization, so it precedes rather than triggers the process.

stem: Which of these is an input to the process of initiating a project, rather than an output of it?
answer: The stage plan for the initiation stage
distractors: The project plan for the whole project
The project initiation documentation
The project authorization request
The full business case
The management approaches
The quality register for the project's products
explanation: The inputs are the authority to initiate, the project brief, the project log, the project product description and the stage plan for the initiation stage, each reviewed or checked. The project plan, business case, management approaches, quality register and project initiation documentation all emerge from the process.

stem: Which management product does this process update rather than create?
answer: The project log
distractors: The business case
The project plan
The management approaches
The project initiation documentation
The project authorization request
The project product description
explanation: The project log is checked as an input and then updated as risks, issues and product register records emerge, and it is the only product shown as updated in the process's output list. The project product description is reviewed rather than listed as an output, although the planning activity may refine it.

stem: Which two processes are triggered by the outputs at the end of initiating a project?
answer: Managing a stage boundary and directing a project
distractors: Starting up a project and directing a project
Directing a project and controlling a stage
Managing a stage boundary and managing product delivery
Controlling a stage and managing a stage boundary
Directing a project and closing a project
Starting up a project and managing a stage boundary
explanation: The stage end approaching output triggers managing a stage boundary, and the project authorization request triggers directing a project, where the board decides whether to authorize the project. Controlling a stage only begins once the project has been authorized.

stem: The project manager should agree with the project board how the management products will be reviewed and approved. Which choice does PRINCE2 describe?
answer: Reviewing each product as it becomes ready, or waiting until the full suite is ready and reviewing it as a set
distractors: Reviewing products only at the end of the project, or delegating review to project assurance
Reviewing products in a formal board meeting, or by written resolution of the executive alone
Reviewing products against the project mandate, or against the outline business case
Reviewing products before they are created, or only after the next stage has started
Reviewing products through change control, or through entries in the daily log
Reviewing products at each programme tranche boundary, or annually, and by the programme manager alone
explanation: Because the project manager creates a suite of management products, the board and project manager must agree whether each product is reviewed as it becomes ready or the whole set is reviewed together. Both are legitimate; what matters is that the arrangement is agreed in advance.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 say that all activities need further consideration when the user-supplier relationship is commercial?
answer: Because the reasons for undertaking the project differ for the user as customer and for the supplier
distractors: Because the supplier becomes accountable for the business case, and the customer for the plan
Because the project board must include a representative of every customer
Because the project must adopt the supplier's management framework, and drop the customer's own
Because tolerances must be agreed with the supplier rather than the board
Because commercial projects cannot apply the principle of managing by exception
Because the business case must be approved by the customer's finance function, and the supplier's
explanation: In a commercial relationship the user is the customer, and the risks, rewards and reasons for doing the project differ between the two parties, so each activity needs further thought. The board's accountability for the business case, and its tolerances, do not move to the supplier.

stem: A business already has a standard project management framework based on a tailored version of PRINCE2. What must the project manager do?
answer: Document and agree how PRINCE2 or the business framework will be applied or tailored for the project
distractors: Apply PRINCE2 in full, because a framework cannot be tailored a second time
Set the business framework aside and tailor PRINCE2 from first principles
Ask the board to choose between the two at the first stage boundary, and apply it then
Adopt the framework unchanged and record any deviations in the daily log
Use the framework for initiation only, then revert to untailored PRINCE2
Leave the choice to project assurance as part of its assurance duties, and the executive's approval
explanation: Tailoring must recognize the internal and external factors affecting delivery, and how PRINCE2 or a business framework will be applied or tailored must be documented and agreed. Using the existing framework is often sensible; ignoring it, or applying PRINCE2 untailored, is not.

stem: Where are the project's tailoring requirements and any related project controls defined?
answer: In the project initiation documentation
distractors: In the project brief
In the stage plan for the initiation stage
In the project log
In the business case
In the project mandate
In the quality register
explanation: A recommended action is to define any tailoring requirements, and the controls that go with them, as part of the project initiation documentation. The project brief may outline a tailoring approach, but the defined requirements belong in the PID.

stem: Which of these is NOT one of the management approaches agreed during initiation?
answer: The resource management approach
distractors: The commercial management approach
The sustainability management approach
The digital and data management approach
explanation: The nine approaches are change, communication, sustainability, benefits, commercial, quality, risk, issue, and digital and data management. Resources are identified within the project plan; there is no separate resource management approach.

stem: Which management approach is recommended to be completed last, and why?
answer: The communication management approach, because it must include the others' communications
distractors: The quality management approach, because it depends on the product descriptions
The risk management approach, because it needs the aggregated risks from the project log
The benefits management approach, because it depends on the project plan
The change management approach, because it needs the baselined project initiation documentation
The commercial management approach, because it depends on the supplier contract
The issue management approach, because it needs the issue register
explanation: Although the approaches can be developed in parallel, communication is best completed last so that it can capture the communication needs arising from all the others. None of the other approaches depends on communication in the same way.

stem: What are the management approaches derived from?
answer: Business strategies, standards or practices to follow, and the users' quality expectations
distractors: The project mandate, the outline business case, and the project plan only
The stage plan for initiation, the project log, and the lessons log from the previous stage
The lessons log, the risk register, and the issue register held by the project support role
The project board's terms of reference, the supplier's contract, and the programme's standard procedures
The product breakdown structure, the product flow diagram, and the work breakdown structure for the stage
The quality register, the issue register, and the daily log kept by the team managers
explanation: The approaches reflect the business strategies, standards or practices the project must comply with, together with the users' quality and sustainability expectations captured in the project product description. The planning products and registers are created later, using the approaches as input.

stem: Which sequencing point does PRINCE2 make about the management approaches?
answer: Once the approaches are defined, the project controls can be established and the project plan created
distractors: The project plan must be created first, because the approaches must reflect its stages
The project controls must be established first, because the approaches must reflect them
The business case must be prepared first, because the approaches must support the justification
The project initiation documentation must be assembled first, because the approaches are extracted from it
The approaches must be approved by the board before any of them can be drafted
The full business case and project plan must both be complete before the approaches are started
explanation: The approaches come before the controls and the plan: once they are defined it becomes possible to establish project controls and create the project plan. This is why agreeing the approaches is placed early in the process.

stem: The project brief records a contractual requirement for the project to follow the customer's change control standard. What effect does this have?
answer: The change management approach must reflect that standard in full
distractors: The requirement is logged and applied only if a change is raised
The requirement is waived because PRINCE2 prescribes its own change approach
The requirement is handled solely by the supplier's commercial management approach
The requirement is added to the project plan as a product to be delivered
The requirement is escalated to the business layer for a decision
The requirement is recorded in the business case as a dis-benefit
explanation: The approaches must reflect any business strategies, standards or practices that apply to the project, expressly including contractual requirements. A contractual standard therefore shapes the relevant approach rather than sitting unused in the log.

stem: Effective project controls are described as a prerequisite for what?
answer: Managing by exception
distractors: Baselining the project initiation documentation
Tailoring PRINCE2 to the project
Appointing the project management team
Preparing the benefits management approach
Closing the project
Agreeing the project mandate
explanation: Delegated authority only works if the board can rely on controls to show when tolerances are threatened, so effective project controls are a prerequisite for managing by exception. Baselining and tailoring are separate steps in the process.

stem: Which of these is listed as an example of a project control?
answer: The number of stages
distractors: The product breakdown structure
The project product description
The communication management approach
The outline business case
The project mandate
The lessons log
explanation: Controls include the frequency and format of communication between management layers, the number of stages, mechanisms to capture and analyze issues, tolerances for delegated authority, monitoring of delegated authority, and mechanisms to escalate exceptions. The others are documents or planning products, not controls.

stem: Many project controls will already have been defined in the management approaches. What is the focus of establishing project controls, then?
answer: Establishing controls and making sure they make sense together as a set
distractors: Defining the controls for the first time in the management approaches
Documenting the controls in the project brief for the board's approval
Delegating the controls to team managers so they can apply them
Replacing the controls with tolerances set by the business layer
Recording the controls in the risk register as risk responses
Confirming the controls with the supplier under the commercial agreement
explanation: Defining a control in an approach is not the same as establishing it, so this activity establishes the controls and checks that together they form a coherent set suited to the project's scale, risk, complexity and importance. The controls must work as a whole, not as isolated mechanisms.

stem: Which task belongs to establishing project controls?
answer: Confirming the delivery method and assessing its implications for project controls
distractors: Writing product descriptions for the project's major products and quality criteria
Updating the outline business case with estimated costs and benefits from the plan
Preparing the project authorization request for the project board and the sponsor
Baselining the project initiation documentation for the project board's approval
Creating the product flow diagram and the product breakdown structure for the plan
Confirming the benefits in the benefits management approach and the review points
explanation: The delivery method, whether linear-sequential, iterative-incremental or hybrid, is confirmed when controls are established because it shapes how the project is controlled. Product descriptions and the product flow diagram belong to preparing the project plan.

stem: Which escalation route does PRINCE2 give when confirming tolerances and escalation procedures?
answer: From team managers to the project manager, from the manager to the board, and from the board to the business
distractors: From the project manager to project assurance, and from project assurance to the project board
From the project board to the project manager, and from the project manager to team managers
From the business layer to the project board, and from the board to the project executive
From team managers to project support, and from project support to the project board, in writing
From the project manager to the project executive only, who then escalates to the business
From the supplier to the senior supplier, and from the senior supplier to the board, in writing
explanation: Tolerances are confirmed for the project and the escalation procedures run up each management layer: team manager to project manager, project manager to project board, and project board to business. Project assurance is a monitoring role, not a step in the escalation route.

stem: Before committing to major expenditure, which requirements must be established, and in which product are they held?
answer: The timescale, resource and people requirements, held in the project plan
distractors: The benefits, dis-benefits and tolerances, held in the business case
The scope, quality criteria and acceptance methods, held in the project product description
The risks, issues and changes, held in the project log
The costs, savings and funding, held in the business case
The roles, responsibilities and authorities, held in the project initiation documentation
The stages, work packages and checkpoints, held in the stage plan
explanation: The project plan holds the timescale, resource and people requirements that must be known before major expenditure is committed, and the board needs it to control the project. The business case holds the justification, not these delivery requirements.

stem: Besides allowing the project board to control the project, what else does the information in the project plan make possible?
answer: Preparing the benefits management approach
distractors: Baselining the project product description
Approving the outline business case
Appointing the project management team
Writing the project mandate
Agreeing the project brief
Preparing the end stage report for initiation
explanation: The plan's timescale, resource and people requirements are needed so that the benefits management approach can be prepared, as well as for board control. The mandate, brief and outline business case all predate initiation.

stem: How does PRINCE2 say the project plan should be produced?
answer: With close involvement of users and suppliers, for example in planning workshops, so it is co-created
distractors: By the project manager alone, then circulated to the team for comment, and approved by the executive
By project support, then approved by the project board without review, and issued to the teams
By the project executive, then reviewed by the project manager, and approved by the project board
By the team managers, once the first delivery stage has been authorized
By project assurance, using lessons from similar projects, and then reviewed by the project manager
By the business layer, applying the organization's standard framework, and approved by the board
explanation: Planning is not something the project manager does in isolation: users and suppliers should be closely involved, and planning workshops help identify the products, their details and the dependencies between them. Project assurance is consulted, but it does not write the plan.

stem: The project product is likely to need maintenance once it is operational. What should the project plan include?
answer: An arrangement such as a service agreement between the support group and the user, planned as a product
distractors: A contingency budget for maintenance held by the project board, and spent by the project manager in the stage
A statement that maintenance is outside the project's scope, and is left to the business to fund
A warranty clause recorded in the commercial management approach, and agreed with the supplier
A separate project to be initiated after the current one closes, and funded by the business
A benefits review scheduled for the end of the product's life, and led by the senior user in the business
An operational stage added to the end of the project lifecycle, and run by the project manager
explanation: Where the product is likely to need maintenance in operation, arrangements for transition should include a suitable service agreement between the support group and the user, and that agreement should appear in the plan as a product. It is not left to a warranty clause or to a later project.

stem: Which set of planning products does PRINCE2 say should be created and included in the project plan?
answer: A product breakdown structure, product descriptions for the major products, and a product flow diagram
distractors: A work breakdown structure, role descriptions for the team, and a resource histogram for the stage
A product checklist, a stage plan for the first stage, and a quality register for the project
A product register, a lessons log for the project, and a risk register for the initiation stage
A product breakdown structure, a business case for the project, and a project initiation documentation
A product flow diagram, a product checklist, and a stage plan for the next delivery stage
A work breakdown structure, a product flow diagram, and a product register for the project plan
explanation: Planning creates a product breakdown structure for the project product and its major components, writes product descriptions for them, and devises a product flow diagram, all included in the project plan. A work breakdown structure is considered under the organizing practice instead.

stem: The project board is the main audience for the project plan. What does PRINCE2 say may be sufficient for presenting the plan to the board?
answer: A product checklist
distractors: A Gantt chart
A product breakdown structure on its own
A product flow diagram
A stage plan for every stage
A work breakdown structure
A highlight report
explanation: The format and presentation of the plan should suit its audience and use, and the manual notes that a product checklist may be enough for presenting the plan to the project board. The full plan remains the baseline even where a summary is used for presentation.

stem: How is the full business case produced from the outline business case?
answer: The outline is updated with the estimated time and costs from the plan and the aggregated risks
distractors: The outline is replaced by a new business case written from the project mandate
The outline is approved unchanged and the detailed figures are held in the project plan, not the case
The full business case is derived from the project initiation documentation once baselined
The outline is kept for the board and a separate full version is written for the supplier
The full business case adds the product descriptions and their quality criteria
The full business case is prepared only where the project sits within a programme
explanation: The full business case develops the outline with the better information available after planning: the estimated time and costs from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the updated project log. It is not a fresh document derived from the mandate or the PID.

stem: Who should be closely involved with the project manager in preparing the full business case?
answer: The project executive
distractors: The senior supplier
The senior user
Project assurance
Project support
The business layer
The team managers
explanation: Preparing the full business case is not done in isolation: it should be co-created with close involvement of the project executive, who is accountable for the justification. Users and suppliers are the key collaborators when the project plan is created.

stem: What will the project board use the full business case for?
answer: To authorize the project, and as the basis of the ongoing check that the project remains viable
distractors: To baseline the project plan and approve the stage tolerances, and release the budget
To confirm the product descriptions and their acceptance criteria, and sign them off
To record the aggregated risks from the project log, and to update the risk register
To appoint the project management team and its role holders, and to approve their objectives
To decide whether to close the project at the next stage boundary, and to record why
To summarize how PRINCE2 has been tailored for the project, and to approve the tailoring
explanation: The board uses the full business case to authorize the project and thereafter as the basis for checking that the project remains viable. It is not the vehicle for tolerances, product criteria or tailoring, which sit elsewhere in the PID.

stem: The project plan shows the work will take longer and cost more than the outline business case assumed. What follows for the business case?
answer: It must be reassessed, because the benefits must still outweigh the revised time, cost and risk
distractors: It is unaffected, because a business case records benefits rather than costs
It is abandoned and the project returns to starting up a project, with a new mandate
It is approved unchanged and the variance is recorded in the project log, with a note to the board
It must be baselined before the project plan is prepared, and approved
It is replaced by the project initiation documentation, which then serves as the case
It is left to the business layer, because the board reviews only benefits, and not costs, or time
explanation: The full business case is built from the plan's estimates precisely because the justification depends on time, cost and aggregated risk as well as on benefits. A material change in those estimates therefore reopens the question of whether the project is still worth doing.

stem: What is the project initiation documentation?
answer: An aggregation of management products created or updated during initiation, used to gain authorization
distractors: A single document containing the project brief and the outline business case
A record of the decisions taken by the project board during the initiation stage
The plan for the initiation stage, approved at the end of starting up a project
A summary of the lessons learned from similar previous projects, and how they were applied by the manager
The formal request to the board to authorize delivery of the project, and release of the funds for it
The set of product descriptions for the project's major products, and their quality criteria
explanation: The PID aggregates many of the products created or updated during initiation and is the means of gaining authorization for the project. The formal request to the board is the project authorization request, which is a separate product.

stem: Which statement about the physical form of the project initiation documentation is correct?
answer: It need not be one document; it may be a collection
distractors: It must be one bound document signed by every member of the project board
It must be held in a project management tool to have any validity
It must be shorter than the project brief it replaces
It must contain a stage plan for every stage of the project
It must be reissued in full at every stage boundary
It must be approved by the business layer before the board sees it
explanation: The PID is defined by what it aggregates rather than by its format: it may be a collection of documents or other information, including a workbook or the contents of a project management tool. Its contents are baselined, but its physical form is flexible.

stem: What must happen to the version of the project initiation documentation used to gain authorization?
answer: It must be baselined and should be placed under change control
distractors: It must be archived immediately and replaced by the first stage plan
It must be approved by project assurance instead of the project board
It must be reviewed only at the end of the project
It must be kept outside change control so that it can be updated freely
It must be summarized in the business case for the board
It must be re-baselined at every progress review
explanation: The authorizing version of the PID must be baselined and should be placed under change control, so that later performance can be compared with the forecasts on which approval was based. Baselining it repeatedly, or leaving it outside change control, would defeat that purpose.

stem: Why is the baselined project initiation documentation retained after authorization?
answer: To compare actual performance against the original forecasts
distractors: To provide the audit trail for the supplier's invoices
To serve as the project mandate for any follow-on project
To record the lessons that emerge during delivery
To replace the business case at each stage boundary
To show the board how the tolerances have been revised
To demonstrate that PRINCE2 has been applied without tailoring
explanation: The baselined PID is the reference point for comparing actual performance with the original forecasts that were approved. Revised tolerances and new lessons are recorded elsewhere, such as in the project log and in progress reports.

stem: Which of these is included or referenced in the project initiation documentation?
answer: The project's management team structure and role descriptions
distractors: The stage plan for the first delivery stage
The project mandate issued by the business layer
The lessons log from similar previous projects
The project manager's daily log, and the project support's notes
A product description for every product in the project
The highlight reports covering the initiation stage
explanation: The PID includes or references the team structure and role descriptions, the business case, the management approaches and the project plan, plus the project controls and a summary of how PRINCE2 has been tailored. Stage plans for later stages are prepared at stage boundaries.

stem: What cross-check is required when assembling the project initiation documentation?
answer: A check that the information in the various elements is compatible
distractors: A check that the PID aligns with the original project mandate
A check that the business case aligns with the benefits management approach
A check that the project plan aligns with the initiation stage plan
A check that the PID complies with the organization's quality management system
A check by the business layer before the board sees the PID
A check that every product description has a matching quality register entry
explanation: Because the PID is assembled from several products, the project manager performs a cross-check that the information in the various elements is compatible. The other checks are not the cross-check described, and alignment with the mandate is not its purpose.

stem: In the final version, which products does the project manager share with the project board when requesting project authorization?
answer: The business case, the project initiation documentation and the project plan
distractors: The project brief, the project mandate and the initiation stage plan
The PID, the product descriptions and the quality register
The full business case, the risk register and the issue register
The project plan, the benefits management approach and the lessons log
The PID, the project log and the product authorization request
The project brief, the outline business case and the project product description
explanation: To finish initiation the project manager shares the final business case, the project initiation documentation and the project plan with the board, because these carry the formal justification. The brief, mandate and outline business case are earlier products.

stem: Why does the project manager formally request project authorization at the end of initiation?
answer: To obtain authority to deliver the project and to secure the people and resources required
distractors: To obtain authority to begin the initiation stage, and to secure its budget and resources
To agree the tolerances for the next stage boundary, and the stage plan for the next stage
To authorize the closure of the project, and to release the team and the budget it holds
To approve the lessons captured during initiation, and to record the actions taken on them
To confirm the appointment of the project manager, and the project management team roles
To approve the initiation stage plan retrospectively, and to authorize the spend already incurred
explanation: The request seeks authority from the board to deliver the project, which is what allows the project manager to secure the people and resources required. Authority to initiate was already given by the board at the start of the process.

stem: How may the activities of initiating a project be applied?
answer: They may be combined, split or run concurrently to suit the project's circumstances
distractors: They must always be performed sequentially in the order shown, without exception
They must be repeated at the start of every management stage
They may be omitted entirely where the project is small, and the board agrees
They must be performed at every stage boundary, and each time the plan changes
They may only be combined where they belong to the same practice
They must be performed by the project board rather than the project manager
explanation: The activities can be combined, split or run concurrently to fit the project's circumstances. This flexibility is part of applying the process, and it does not mean that the process can be skipped.

stem: Some projects are too complex for the full output to be defined by the end of initiation. What does PRINCE2 say is common in such cases?
answer: A lifecycle with investigative stages to examine options, initiating used only at the start
distractors: Delaying initiation until the full output has been defined in the project brief
Running initiating a project again at the start of every investigative stage
Splitting the work into separate projects, each with its own PID
Baselining the PID with the project's output left undefined, and the board approving it in full
Adopting a linear-sequential lifecycle to force early definition of the output
Asking the business layer to define the output in the project mandate
explanation: Where the output cannot be fully defined, a lifecycle with investigative stages is common, and initiating a project is used only at the start of the first stage to establish the management and control environment. Re-running initiation at every stage would defeat the purpose of the process.

stem: The number of management products in this process can look daunting. What guidance does PRINCE2 give?
answer: Start simple and elaborate if needed, rather than create an environment suited to a hypothetical project
distractors: Create every product in full, then remove those the board does not want, and the executive agrees
Use the product set from the largest similar project as a template, and tailor it down at once
Ask the programme office to produce all the products before initiation begins
Reduce the products to the project brief and the business case only, and drop the rest
Decide the tailoring only at the first stage boundary, and apply it from the second stage
Delegate the choice of products to project assurance, and the project board's approval
explanation: Tailoring factors may not be clear at the start of initiation, so the guidance is to begin simply and elaborate as needs emerge. Building a management environment for a hypothetical major project risks unnecessary overhead.

stem: Which statement about roles in initiating a project is correct?
answer: The project manager answers to the executive for running the project and may assign roles as suitable
distractors: The project executive creates all the management products for the project manager to approve
Project support is accountable to the board for the products it creates
The project board assigns each activity to a named member of the project team
Project assurance creates the management products and the project manager reviews them
The business layer must write the business case because it owns the benefits
The senior supplier is responsible for the project plan because it commits resources
explanation: The project manager is responsible to the executive for how the project is run and can assign the roles to whoever is appropriate, with project support often producing some of the supporting products. Accountability for those products does not move to project support or assurance.

stem: In the RACI chart for initiating a project, which activity has the project manager accountable and project support responsible?
answer: Assembling the project initiation documentation
distractors: Preparing the project plan for the project board
Preparing the full business case for the board
Establishing project controls for the stage
Agreeing the management approaches with the board
Agreeing tailoring requirements with the executive
Requesting project authorization from the board
explanation: Assembling the PID is the activity where the project manager is accountable rather than responsible, with project support responsible for doing the assembly. For the other activities the project executive is accountable and the project manager is responsible.

stem: In the RACI chart for initiating a project, which role is accountable for most of the activities?
answer: The project executive
distractors: The project manager
The business layer
The senior user
The senior supplier
Project assurance
Project support
explanation: The executive is accountable for agreeing tailoring, agreeing the approaches, establishing controls, preparing the plan, preparing the full business case and requesting authorization. The project manager is responsible for those activities, and project support is responsible for assembling the PID.

stem: According to the application of the practices, how is the risk register created during initiation?
answer: Based on the categories and grading system defined in the risk management approach
distractors: From the risks listed in the project brief, regardless of category
By the project board when it authorizes the project, and in the first board meeting
From the daily log once delivery of the first stage begins
By project assurance during its review of the project initiation documentation
From the aggregated risks recorded in the business case only
By the senior supplier for supplier-related risks only, and the executive for others
explanation: The risk register is created using the categories and grading system set out in the risk management approach, with risks from the business case, the project plan and elsewhere logged and assessed. The approach comes first; the register then applies it.

stem: Which report is used to show progress for the initiation stage?
answer: A highlight report
distractors: A checkpoint report
An end stage report
An exception report
A lessons report
A product status account
An issue report
explanation: The manual notes that highlight reports are used to show progress for the initiation stage, as they are for other stages. Checkpoint reports come from team managers, and end stage reports are produced at stage boundaries.

stem: Which two management approaches are developed to support the business case and provide input for establishing controls?
answer: The benefits management approach and the sustainability management approach
distractors: The commercial management approach and the quality management approach
The risk management approach and the issue management approach
The change management approach and the communication management approach
The digital and data management approach and the quality management approach
The commercial management approach and the change management approach
The communication management approach and the benefits management approach
explanation: Under the business case practice, the benefits management approach and the sustainability management approach are developed to support the business case and feed into establishing controls. The risk, issue, change and communication approaches support other practices.
